at-0001.title: Round money only via round_money
at-0001.content: Always round monetary Decimal results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

review_comments: [team convention] Round money only with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent). Python's round() and a bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and give wrong invoice totals.

last_failure.review_comment: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

at-0002.title: Normalize money via to_money and round_money
at-0002.content: In ledgerly/invoice.py, convert any monetary input with to_money() and store it rounded with round_money() before constructing LineItem; compare against ZERO from ledgerly.money rather than a literal.

at-0003.title: Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes
at-0003.content: Reject invalid input by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly.errors with the established codes: "invalid_state" for wrong invoice status, "invalid_quantity" for bad quantity, "negative_amount" for negative money.

            "invalid_tax_rate", f"tax rate must be between 0 and 100, got {rate}"

at-0004.title: Exclude bool when validating integer fields
at-0004.content: When validating integer arguments such as quantity, check isinstance(x, bool) first because bool is a subclass of int, then require isinstance(x, int) and a positive value.
